questions.q: What two things, together, make a component appear as a choice in Lightning App Builder?
options: A .css file and a __tests__ folder
isExposed set to true, and a <targets> list naming at least one valid surface
An @api property and a slot
A master-detail relationship on the object
questions.explain: isExposed must be true before a component can appear anywhere outside its own project, and <targets> then lists exactly which surfaces (record page, app page, home page) it should appear on.

questions.q: Which target allows a component to be placed on a custom Lightning Home page?
options: lightning__RecordPage
lightning__AppPage
lightning__HomePage
lightning__Tab
questions.explain: lightning__HomePage specifically makes a component available for placement on a custom Lightning Home page, distinct from lightning__RecordPage (record detail pages) and lightning__AppPage (app pages).

questions.q: What does a <targetConfig>'s <property> element actually do?
options: It declares a brand-new field on the underlying Salesforce object
It exposes a matching @api property as a field an admin can set visually inside Lightning App Builder, with its type determining the kind of input control rendered
It sets the component's CSS styling for that target
It controls which users can view the component at runtime
questions.explain: A property entry inside targetConfigs turns a plain @api property (otherwise only settable from another component's JavaScript) into an admin-configurable field in App Builder, with its type attribute determining the input control (checkbox, text field, etc.).

questions.q: What does the <objects> element inside a lightning__RecordPage targetConfig control?
options: Which Apex classes the component is allowed to call
Which object's record pages the component can be dropped onto -- restricting it, for example, to only Case records
The order components appear in within App Builder's component panel
Whether the component can be deployed to production at all
questions.explain: The <objects> element restricts a lightning__RecordPage component to specific object types. Leaving it out makes the component available on every object's record page instead.

questions.q: What happens to an @api property on a component's class that has no matching <property> entry in any <targetConfig>?
options: The component fails to deploy
It remains settable by another component's JavaScript (parent-to-child, per Lesson 10), but an admin cannot configure it visually inside App Builder
It is automatically removed from the class at compile time
It becomes a required field that must be set before deployment
questions.explain: An @api property works for parent-to-child JavaScript communication regardless of targetConfigs. It only becomes an admin-configurable field in App Builder once a matching <property> entry exposes it there.
